label: Digitally Immersed & Emotionally Distressed
summary: This profile represents highly educated women who spend more than 5 hours daily online and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Their UCLA-8 loneliness score (1.74), PHQ-9 depression score (1.75), and GAD-7 anxiety score (2.17) all sit in the higher range, suggesting a pattern of co-occurring emotional distress. With 165 respondents in this cluster, it reflects a substantial subgroup where extended screen time coincides with pronounced psychological burden.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, daily screen/internet use exceeding 5 hours
behavior_markers: Extended daily digital engagement (more than 5 hours)
Co-occurring depressive and anxiety symptoms at above-average levels
High educational attainment paired with significant emotional distress
Pattern suggesting possible social isolation despite digital immersion
tone: Concerned and empathetic, highlighting the intersection of high digital engagement and emotional vulnerability

label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report lower levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms compared to other groups. With UCLA-8 loneliness, PHQ-9 depression, and GAD-7 anxiety scores all well below scale midpoints, these individuals demonstrate consistently positive psychological well-being across all three measured dimensions.
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate-level education or above, 1–3 hours of daily screen/internet use
behavior_markers: Reports minimal loneliness (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 0.77, near floor)
Exhibits very low depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.33)
Maintains moderate and limited daily screen or internet use (1–3 hours)
Demonstrates consistently low distress across all psychological measures

label: Lonely but Emotionally Resilient
summary: This profile captures respondents who report notably elevated loneliness yet maintain relatively low levels of depressive and anxiety symptoms. Despite feeling socially disconnected, they do not exhibit the affective distress typically associated with loneliness, suggesting a degree of emotional resilience or effective coping that buffers against mood and anxiety disorders.
demographic_anchor: Predominantly female, holding graduate-level education or above, reporting 1–3 hours of daily screen/social-media use
behavior_markers: Elevated loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.30) indicating moderate-to-high perceived social isolation
Low depressive symptom burden (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.86) suggesting minimal clinical depression
Low anxiety symptom levels (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.91) indicating limited generalized anxiety
Moderate daily screen or social-media engagement (1–3 hours), neither extremely low nor high
Possible reliance on internal coping strategies that decouple loneliness from mood deterioration
tone: Quietly disconnected yet psychologically stable; socially under-nourished but not emotionally overwhelmed
